title: Parameters of the worked example: net field demand to boundary-specific gross requirements

dataset.name: Gone Abat Jap open-canal irrigation network, 16-period version (am2a)
dataset.demand_meaning: net field irrigation requirement per terminal, m3 per dekad
dataset.positions_meaning: x coordinate of node_positions is the picket (chainage) along the main canal; y is a drawing offset only

variants.source: author decision, 2026-11-10: terminal edges are earthen canals of unknown length, so the dataset efficiencies are the primary case and the short-edge efficiency rule is a sensitivity case

short_picket_threshold_m.description: sensitivity variant "rule" only: terminal edges whose picket difference is below this value receive the length-proportional efficiency

eta_short_max.description: sensitivity variant "rule" only: efficiency assigned to the shortest edge of the short group

eta_short_min.description: sensitivity variant "rule" only: efficiency assigned to the longest edge of the short group

outlets_at_junction.description: sensitivity variant "rule" only: terminals whose outlet is placed at the picket of their junction node, because their drawn x value is a layout position

eta_a.description: field application efficiency, the same for all terminals
eta_a.source: Nominal and lower bound: Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 798: average field application ratio 0.43, range 0.37-0.47 for silt loam and silty clay loam soils (Shomakhulum WUA, Khorezm). Upper bound: Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 77: application efficiency of 50% in an 850-ha sub-unit in Khorezm (field observations 40-50%, p. 75). The FAO indicative value of 60% for surface irrigation (Brouwer, Prins, Heibloem 1989, Training manual no. 4, Annex I, Table 8) and the improved-practice targets of 0.65-0.67 (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 87; Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 800) lie above the current-conditions range.

edge_loss_rel_halfwidth.description: relative half-width of the uniform uncertainty of every edge loss fraction 1 - eta_e; the nominal eta_e comes from the dataset or the short-edge rule
edge_loss_rel_halfwidth.source: Of the order of the spread of conveyance efficiencies reported in the reviewed studies: 51% (Gilsha Bai E.B., Rema K.P., Joseph A., Sathian K.K. (2023) JAEI 60, 74-85, doi:10.52151/jae2023601.1798) and 74% (Melsse D.W., Tegegne M.A., Ayele T.M. (2025) Appl. Water Sci. 15, 300, doi:10.1007/s13201-025-02659-z), i.e. losses of 0.26-0.49, about +/-31% around their midpoint. Ponding tests in Khorezm gave losses of about 5% of the discharge per 100 m in small canals of low hierarchy and much lower losses in larger canals (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 86).

phi_E.description: share of edge losses that evaporates from the canal water surface (consumed)
phi_E.source: Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 798: about 3% of the irrigation losses evaporate, about 7% go directly to the drains as operational losses and 90% recharge the aquifer (lower Amu Darya, Khorezm). The partition is given there for total losses; it is applied here to canal losses. Range assumed.

phi_O.description: share of edge losses that leaves as operational spills
phi_O.source: Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 798: about 7% of the irrigation losses go directly to the drains as operational losses. Range assumed, because operational losses are hard to quantify (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 87).

rho_S.description: fraction of canal seepage that is recoverable within the basin
rho_S.source: No study quantifies the recoverable fraction for the lower Amu Darya. Context: drainage outflow is 55-67% of the irrigation input (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, pp. 76 and 85; Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); re-use of drainage water is limited by its salinity of 2.0-2.5 g/l (Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); capillary rise from shallow groundwater supplies 16-33% of crop evapotranspiration (Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 800; Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2014) Irrig. Sci. 32, 449-458, doi:10.1007/s00271-014-0441-5, p. 457; Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 85). The full admissible range is therefore kept, with its midpoint as the nominal value.

rho_O.description: fraction of operational spills that is recoverable within the basin
rho_O.source: No study quantifies the recoverable fraction for the lower Amu Darya. Context: drainage outflow is 55-67% of the irrigation input (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, pp. 76 and 85; Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); re-use of drainage water is limited by its salinity of 2.0-2.5 g/l (Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); capillary rise from shallow groundwater supplies 16-33% of crop evapotranspiration (Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. Sci. 31, 793-806, doi:10.1007/s00271-012-0362-0, p. 800; Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2014) Irrig. Sci. 32, 449-458, doi:10.1007/s00271-014-0441-5, p. 457; Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, p. 85). The full admissible range is therefore kept, with its midpoint as the nominal value.

rho_F.description: fraction of field losses (deep percolation and runoff) that is recoverable within the basin
rho_F.source: No study quantifies the recoverable fraction for the lower Amu Darya. Context: drainage outflow is 55-67% of the irrigation input (Tischbein B. et al. (2012) in: Cotton, Water, Salts and Soums, Springer, 69-92, doi:10.1007/978-94-007-1963-7_5, pp. 76 and 85; Conrad C. et al. (2013) Phys. Chem. Earth 61-62, 52-62, doi:10.1016/j.pce.2013.05.002, p. 59); capillary rise from shallow groundwater supplies 16-33% of crop evapotranspiration (Awan U.K., Tischbein B., Martius C. (2013) Irrig. delta_S.description: change of water stored in the canals over a dekad
delta_S.source: Neglected at the dekad scale (model, section 5); stated as an assumption in the article.

temporal.reference_flow: seasonal mean inflow discharge of each edge in the linear model

canal_bed_soil.source: Cadastral data (passport) of the Kizketken canal system, table of actual canal parameters, row "soils on sections" for the Kegeyli canal (unpublished; authors' archive). The Kegeyli canal soil is used for the main canal of the worked example (authors' information, 2026-11-11).

kostiakov_m.description: exponent of the discharge dependence of seepage losses (seepage fraction proportional to Q^-m)
kostiakov_m.source: Nominal 0.5: Kostiakov A.N. (1960) Osnovy melioratsii [Fundamentals of land reclamation], 6th ed., Sel'khozgiz, Moscow, pp. 187-188: seepage loss sigma = A/Q^m, in percent of the discharge per km of canal, with Q in m3/s; canals in light soils A = 3.4, m = 0.5 (author's data); observations of SANIIRI on canals in Central Asia give m = 0.5 for light, medium and heavy soils (A = 2.85-3.5, 1.87-2.3 and 1.0-1.3). The canal bed is sand and sandy loam (see canal_bed_soil), a light soil. Sensitivity 0.45: Syed N.S.B., Zhao S. (2023) J. Water Land Dev. 57, 21-29, doi:10.24425/jwld.2023.145332, pp. 23-24: permeability index 0.45 of the Kostiakov formula for silt clay loam (SCL) canal bed soil (after Zhang et al., 2017).
